trust_decision.summary: networkInterfaces() decides on Linux whether an interface is DHCP by reading interfaces(5) config; the trust boundary is the `source <path>` field of that file, which checkLinuxDCHPInterfaces interpolates into a shell command at lib/network.js:551, so a path carrying shell metacharacters is executed by the library process.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the interfaces(5) source-directive path; searching the pinned tree for '/etc/network' lands on the hardcoded call at lib/network.js:584, whose callee builds `cat ${file} | grep` from the `source` field at lib/network.js:562.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No unpatched sibling exists to attach a dismissal to; the only argument available is aimed at the fixed site itself - that /etc/network/interfaces is root-owned config, so a `source` path is trusted - which is exactly the argument the advisory rejects.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The recursive `source <pattern>` include: interfaces(5) allows globs (the Debian default is `source /etc/network/interfaces.d/*`), which the old `cat ${file}` let the shell expand. readFileSync of the literal glob path throws ENOENT, so the published fix silently drops every DHCP iface declared under interfaces.d; a correct fix must readdir/glob, not only remove the shell. The old `2> /dev/null` also tolerated unreadable files, which readFileSync turns into a throwing call.

O6_input_shapes: the hardcoded absolute path the library passes itself (`/etc/network/interfaces`)
a path taken verbatim from field 1 of a `source` directive (relative or absolute)
a path containing shell metacharacters, spaces or quotes
a path containing a glob (`/etc/network/interfaces.d/*`), which the old shell expanded

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a `source`-directive include that expands globs (what ifupdown actually does) with an extra branch per pattern
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The current code already takes field 1 of the `source` line and recurses on it; adding the documented glob support would most naturally be written as `execSync('cat ' + pattern)`, recreating the identical sink one line away from the fixed one.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second config location read the same way (`/etc/network/interfaces.d`, /etc/NetworkManager/system-connections keyfiles)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The library hardcodes one config path and shells `cat ... | grep` over it; extending DHCP detection to a distro that keeps the file elsewhere copies the same call with a different constant, and the next path could come from the environment or a user option.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another `cat /sys/class/net/${iface}/...` probe for a new sysfs field or for a bridge/VLAN config file
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The maintainer's idiom throughout this file is a single execSync string with `${ifaceSanitized}` interpolated; a new probe added next to the existing 24-line one would follow the same shape, and sanitizeString only covers values the library itself derived, not values read from a file.

O9_family: OS command injection (CWE-78): shell string built from interfaces(5) config content and passed to execSync

O10_build.toolchain: plain node >= 8 (package.json engines); no build step and no runtime dependencies; optional biome/eslint config files only
O10_build.project_tests: test/test.js is the npm test entry (package.json:15); CI runs test/ci.js (.github/workflows/test.yml:37), which exercises si.networkInterfaces() at test/ci.js:74-75. No test covers checkLinuxDCHPInterfaces or the interfaces(5) parsing, and the fix adds or changes no test source.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Keep execSync and wrap the interpolated value in util.sanitizeString(file) - the idiom every neighbouring call in this file already uses (lib/network.js:540, 825, 941) - which strips `; | $ \` *` (lib/util.js:713-743), passes an injection test with a metacharacter path, and still mangles or drops legitimate glob/relative source paths.

out_of_scope_notes: lib/filesystem.js:488 interpolates a block-device name taken from lsblk output into `mdadm --export --detail /dev/${element.name}` - the same CWE-78 family but a different sink and outside this advisory's protection; not pursued.

lib/network.js:368-377 getWindowsWirelessIfaceSSID builds `netsh wlan show interface name="..."` from its argument at lib/network.js:370, but the only caller passes the already-sanitized value (lib/network.js:1141) and it is a Windows route outside this Linux advisory; noted, not pursued.

docs/security.html:47-58 at the pinned commit documents the previous round of this same function (CVE-2026-44724, fixed by parameter checking plus execFile in 5.31.6); the pinned release is that incomplete defence, which is why this follow-up advisory exists.
